native_rules: Bits advance least-significant first; fields are not implicitly byte-aligned.
Bounded integers use a value-dependent mask/valueSoFar stop condition.
Packed uint32 uses bit0 for continuation and bits1..7 for each payload group; 255 encodes ff02.
Packet notify packs a 14-bit sequence, 14-bit ACK and four-bit history count minus one, followed by history DWORDs.
The native notify reader reads min(advertisedHistoryWords,8). The local canonical profile rejects advertised 9..16.
Connection+b8 is always serialized as one bunch-header bit; ordinary reliable connections serialize a ten-bit channel sequence.
Control hardcoded name ID255 comes from the native registration/lookup tables, independently of the captured Hello boundary.
The legacy Hello-only probe remains available. The admission connection implements Hello0, Challenge3, four-field Login5, Welcome1, Netspeed4 and Join9 with native reliable channel sequences.
Login5's literal Response0 and explicit empty delegated identity are not credentials; the connection checks only the local lobby-issued Cookie plus player, room and map bindings.
MatchPlayerInfo.field24 ds_token is the client's GetLevelUrl Cookie source. It is distinct from top-level secret_key19 and team_id13.
Welcome for map2201 uses Iris_Entry, observed as the persistent FURL.Map in the same official Dam match. Original Welcome bytes and local native acceptance remain unverified.
Reliable delivery requires the exact packet-history bit for a recorded transmission. Cursor movement or an unrelated nonzero history bit cannot clear the outbox.
Timer retries retain reliable control content and channel sequence, use a new packet sequence, and cannot refresh client activity. Empty ACK-only packets do not trigger ACK ping-pong.

New Login cannot precede a sent Challenge; new Netspeed/Join cannot precede a sent Welcome. Unsupported inbound messages, partial bunches, encryption tokens, GUID exports, actor replication and gameplay state remain rejected by the control connection without a delivery ACK.
Reliable retry digests are bounded to the last128 consumed channel sequences; a new expected sequence advances even after a full1024-value wrap with identical payloads.
Challenge and Welcome payloads are both preflighted in the complete native packet envelope, including maximal sequence/name fields.

The internal initial Actor-open producer is opt-in after a ticket-authorized Join; default Join does not create or send an Actor. GUID graph membership and declared reference resolvability do not prove native object resolution.

Each new Actor channel uses the saved original server reliable seed+1. Initial opens on at most16 channels share the packet allocator/reply budget with Control, keep every bunch bit stable on retransmission, and require an exact ACK history bit. Delivered channels and dynamic GUIDs cannot reopen within that generation.

Actor content blocks follow the Actor-open and any explicitly selected base PlayerController index tail without alignment: RepLayout bit, true Actor selector, packed payload bit count and exact opaque body. Derived PlayerController headers and actual property/RPC bodies remain unimplemented.

Normal non-internal-ACK class-field envelopes now encode a bounded RepIndex using an explicitly supplied class-cache exclusive maximum, packed payload bit length and exact opaque body. Index0 and zero-length fields are not sequence terminators; body EOF bounds the sequence. False-RepLayout wrapping composes with Actor transport, but no real game field mapping, property serializer, possession or RPC is supplied.

Offline supplied class-cache snapshots validate48-byte headers and32-byte entries with inherited contiguous indices and bounded parent chains. Their maximum derives from the complete chain plus one; the final encodable sentinel has no descriptor. This decoder is not a runtime exporter or actual game-class schema. Ordinary cached-field envelopes do not replace the separate RepLayout command stream.
